note: A small, wide comparison table — 44 rows, 51 columns, one row per provider x plan.
It is here for two things the jobs file cannot test: an outcome with only nine
distinct values (a flat 'fewer than twelve means category' rule rejected it, and
that rule was wrong), and a table where the honest answer to 'which provider is
best' is that 44 rows across 12 providers cannot support one. The deck is
expected to recognise the outcome and still decline to rank on it.
